s:
Consider the following statements regarding medieval Persian chronicles:
1. Taj-ul-Maasir was written by Hasan Nizami and relates to the early Sultanate.
2. Hasan Nizami was patronised by Qutbuddin Aibak.
3. Tabaqat-i-Nasiri was dedicated to Nasiruddin Mahmud.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. Taj-ul-Maasir is associated with Hasan Nizami and the early Sultanate, while Tabaqat-i-Nasiri was dedicated to Nasiruddin Mahmud.
tq: Combine author, patron and dedication facts while checking whether all statements belong to the same source cluster.
sec: Persian and Arabic chronicles → author + reign covered + chronological order

s: Tabaqat-i-Nasiri primarily deals with which of the following periods?
o: The Bahmani rulers and the Qutb Shahis
The reigns of the later Mughals
The Ghurids and the early Delhi Sultans
The reigns of Akbar and Jahangir
x: Minhaj-us-Siraj’s Tabaqat-i-Nasiri covers the Ghurids and the early Delhi Sultans.
tq: Use the period covered as the distinguishing clue when several Sultanate works are listed.
sec: Persian and Arabic chronicles → author + reign covered + chronological order

s: Who wrote Futuh-us-Salatin, a work covering the Ghaznavids to Muhammad bin Tughlaq and written at the Bahmani court around 1350?
x: Futuh-us-Salatin was written by Isami at the Bahmani court around 1350 and covers the period from the Ghaznavids to Muhammad bin Tughlaq, including the Tughlaq campaigns against Warangal.
tq: Distinguish similar Sultanate historians by matching the work with its author and historical range.
sec: Persian and Arabic chronicles → author + reign covered + chronological order

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi — Yahiya bin Ahmad Sarhindi
x: Tabaqat-i-Akbari was written by Nizamuddin Ahmad. Badauni’s own historical work was Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh.
tq: Find the wrong author–work pairing, especially where a neighbouring historian is substituted.
sec: Persian and Arabic chronicles → author + reign covered + chronological order

s: Fatawa-i-Jahandari is primarily a work on which subject?
o: The postal system of the Delhi Sultanate
x: Fatawa-i-Jahandari, written by Ziauddin Barani, deals with political theory and kingship.
tq: Identify the subject of a text rather than confusing it with the author’s historical chronicle.
sec: Persian and Arabic chronicles → author + reign covered + chronological order

s: Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi was written during the reign of which ruler?
o: Mubarak Shah of the Sayyid dynasty
Nasiruddin Mahmud of the Slave dynasty
x: Yahiya bin Ahmad Sarhindi wrote Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi during the reign of Sayyid Sultan Mubarak Shah.
tq: Use the title and reign association to separate similarly named Sultanate chronicles.
sec: Persian and Arabic chronicles → author + reign covered + chronological order

s:
Arrange the following works in chronological order of the periods they primarily cover:
A. Tabaqat-i-Akbari
B. Taj-ul-Maasir
C. Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi
D. Tabaqat-i-Nasiri
x: Taj-ul-Maasir belongs to the early Sultanate, followed by Tabaqat-i-Nasiri, Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi and finally Tabaqat-i-Akbari up to Akbar’s reign.
tq: Place the earliest and latest works first, then distinguish the two intervening Sultanate chronicles.
sec: Persian and Arabic chronicles → author + reign covered + chronological order

s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding Amir Khusrau?
o: He wrote Kitab-ul-Yamini as court historian of Mahmud of Ghazni.
He wrote Rihla in Arabic after visiting Muhammad bin Tughlaq’s court.
He wrote Shahnama under the patronage of Akbar.
He wrote Khazain-ul-Futuh and accompanied Malik Kafur’s 1310 invasion of Warangal.
x: Amir Khusrau, court poet of Alauddin Khalji, wrote Khazain-ul-Futuh and accompanied Malik Kafur’s 1310 expedition to Warangal. Kitab-ul-Yamini was written by Utbi, Shahnama by Firdausi and Rihla by Ibn Battuta.
tq: Apply the author–ruler–work trap to distinguish famous medieval writers.
sec: Persian and Arabic chronicles → author + reign covered + chronological order

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Utbi was the court historian of Mahmud of Ghazni and wrote Kitab-ul-Yamini. Firdausi wrote Shahnama, Ibn Battuta wrote Rihla and Amir Khusrau wrote Khazain-ul-Futuh.
tq: Use the famous title as the anchor and reject swapped authors.
sec: Persian and Arabic chronicles → author + reign covered + chronological order

s: Rihla, the travel account of Ibn Battuta, was written in which language?
x: Ibn Battuta’s travel account, Rihla, was written in Arabic.
tq: Test the exact language of a source rather than its author’s place of origin.
sec: Persian and Arabic chronicles → author + reign covered + chronological order

s: Marco Polo, who landed at Motupalli, visited the kingdom of which ruler?
x: Marco Polo visited the Kakatiya kingdom during the reign of Rudramadevi in 1289–93 and landed at Motupalli.
tq: Link the traveller’s landing place with the ruler and kingdom visited.
sec: Foreign travellers → country of origin + ruler visited + subject described

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Ibn Battuta — Morocco — Muhammad bin Tughlaq
Abdur Razzaq — Portugal — Deva Raya II
x: Ibn Battuta was from Morocco and visited the court of Muhammad bin Tughlaq. Marco Polo was from Venice, Abdur Razzaq from Persia and Duarte Barbosa from Portugal.
tq: Begin with the country–traveller pair and verify the ruler visited.
sec: Foreign travellers → country of origin + ruler visited + subject described

s: Which traveller is associated with observations on espionage, the postal system, sati and slave markets in the Delhi Sultanate?
x: Ibn Battuta’s account of Muhammad bin Tughlaq’s reign contains observations on espionage, the postal system, sati and slave markets.
tq: Match the distinctive subject described with the traveller who recorded it.
sec: Foreign travellers → country of origin + ruler visited + subject described

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Nicolo Conti was a traveller from Venice.
2. He described innumerable oil lamps at Diwali in Vijayanagara.
3. The APPSC-associated account places him at the court of Deva Raya II.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct in the stated account. Nicolo Conti was a Venetian traveller associated with Vijayanagara and is noted for describing innumerable oil lamps at Diwali.
tq: Combine origin, court and distinctive observation to identify one traveller precisely.
sec: Foreign travellers → country of origin + ruler visited + subject described

s: Who among the following mentioned that Vijayanagara possessed more than 300 port towns?
x: Duarte Barbosa, the Portuguese traveller, is associated with the observation that Vijayanagara had more than 300 port towns.
tq: Use the distinctive numerical detail to separate travellers with otherwise similar Vijayanagara accounts.
sec: Foreign travellers → country of origin + ruler visited + subject described

s: Abdur Razzaq visited Vijayanagara in 1443–44 as an envoy sent by which ruler?
x: Abdur Razzaq was a Persian envoy of Shah Rukh and visited the court of Deva Raya II in 1443–44.
tq: Distinguish the envoy’s sending ruler from the ruler whose court he visited.
sec: Foreign travellers → country of origin + ruler visited + subject described

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Seydi Ali Reis — Italy — Ottoman admiral
Mahmud Wali Balkhi — Balkh — Qutb Shahi court
Mir Zainul Abidin — Persia — Muhammad Qutb Shah
x: Seydi Ali Reis was from Turkey and was an Ottoman admiral, not from Italy. Tavernier was French, Mir Zainul Abidin was Persian and Mahmud Wali Balkhi came from Balkh.
tq: Find the incorrect country–traveller association among closely related foreign visitors.
sec: Foreign travellers → country of origin + ruler visited + subject described

s: Robert Sewell’s A Forgotten Empire is based principally on the accounts of which group?
o: Barbosa, Seydi Ali Reis and Mahmud Wali Balkhi
Marco Polo, Ibn Battuta and Tavernier
x: Robert Sewell’s A Forgotten Empire draws chiefly on the accounts of Paes, Nuniz and Abdur Razzaq.
tq: Recognise the specific cluster of sources associated with a modern historical reconstruction.
sec: Foreign travellers → country of origin + ruler visited + subject described

s: Al-Biruni came to India in approximately which year and century?
o: Around 1030 CE in the eleventh century
Around 1450 CE in the fifteenth century
Around 1300 CE in the fourteenth century
Around 1150 CE in the twelfth century
x: Al-Biruni came to India around 1030 CE, during the eleventh century, under Mahmud of Ghazni.
tq: Distinguish the century and approximate date using the middle-period historical sequence.
sec: Al-Biruni - century, patron, works, views on India

s: Which one of the following statements about Al-Biruni is correct?
o: He confined his study of India exclusively to military campaigns.
He wrote in Persian without learning any Indian language.
He was patronised by Deva Raya II of Vijayanagara.
He wrote in Arabic after learning Sanskrit and studied Indian religion, philosophy, astronomy and caste.
x: Al-Biruni learned Sanskrit and wrote in Arabic on Indian religion, philosophy, astronomy and the caste system. He was associated with Mahmud of Ghazni, not Vijayanagara.
tq: Use the language, subjects and patron together to identify the correct biographical statement.
sec: Al-Biruni - century, patron, works, views on India

s: According to Al-Biruni’s account, which of the following was observed on Kartika Amavasya?
o: The conquest of Madurai by Kampana
The coronation of Muhammad bin Tughlaq
The annual court of the Qutb Shahis
x: Al-Biruni recorded the celebration of Diwali on Kartika Amavasya.
tq: Match the festival and its calendrical occasion with the appropriate chronicler.
sec: Al-Biruni - century, patron, works, views on India

s: Which one of the following was Al-Biruni’s observation about Indian society?
o: Indians had abandoned Sanskrit learning entirely.
Indian society was free from caste distinctions.
Indians were unwilling to share learning with outsiders.
Indian scholars refused to study astronomy.
x: Al-Biruni observed that Indians were unwilling to share their learning with outsiders. He nevertheless studied Indian religion, philosophy, astronomy and caste through Sanskrit sources.
tq: Identify the precise social observation without reversing its meaning.
sec: Al-Biruni - century, patron, works, views on India

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Ramacharitam — Sandhyakara Nandi — Life of Ramapala
Prithviraja Vijaya — Gangadevi — Life of Prithviraj Chauhan
Madhura Vijayam — Jayanaka — Conquest of Madurai
x: Ramacharitam was written by Sandhyakara Nandi and deals with the life of Pala king Ramapala. Prithviraja Vijaya was by Jayanaka, Madhura Vijayam by Gangadevi and Siddhesvara Charitam by Kase Siddhappa.
tq: Start with the author–work pair and check the subject attached to each regional source.
sec: Regional and Sanskrit sources - Rajatarangini, biographies, Vijayanagara and Qutb Shahi works

s: Madhura Vijayam provides information chiefly about which of the following?
o: Kampana’s conquest of Madurai and conditions under Tughlaq rule
The conquest of Golconda by Aurangzeb
The life of Pala king Ramapala
x: Madhura Vijayam, written by Gangadevi, describes Kampana’s conquest of Madurai and conditions under Tughlaq rule.
tq: Associate the regional biography with its protagonist, campaign and political context.
sec: Regional and Sanskrit sources - Rajatarangini, biographies, Vijayanagara and Qutb Shahi works

s: Siddhesvara Charitam, written in Telugu by Kase Siddhappa, is a source for the study of which subject?
x: Siddhesvara Charitam is a Telugu work by Kase Siddhappa that provides information on Kakatiya-era society and religion.
tq: Match the language and author with the regional historical theme.
sec: Regional and Sanskrit sources - Rajatarangini, biographies, Vijayanagara and Qutb Shahi works

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Tarikh-i-Firishta — Muhammad Qasim Firishta — Deccan history
Hadikat-us-Salatin — Ali bin Tahir Bustani — Qutb Shahis
Kumara Ramana Charitam — Kannada — South India after the fall of Warangal
x: Muntakhab-ul-Lubab was written by Khafi Khan and deals with Aurangzeb’s conquest of Golconda. Gangadevi wrote Madhura Vijayam.
tq: Detect the swapped author in a list of regional and Deccan sources.
sec: Regional and Sanskrit sources - Rajatarangini, biographies, Vijayanagara and Qutb Shahi works

s: Tarikh-i-Firishta is also known as which of the following?
x: Tarikh-i-Firishta is also called Gulshan-i-Ibrahimi and was written by Muhammad Qasim Firishta.
tq: Discriminate between similar Persian titles by identifying the alternate title of the same work.
sec: Regional and Sanskrit sources - Rajatarangini, biographies, Vijayanagara and Qutb Shahi works

s:
Which of the following statements regarding Muhammad Qasim Firishta is correct?
1. He was born in Astarabad in Iran.
2. He was born in 1552.
3. His work calls Telangana ‘Tilang’.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. Firishta was born at Astarabad in Iran in 1552, and his Deccan history refers to Telangana as ‘Tilang’.
tq: Combine biographical numbers with a distinctive terminology clue.
sec: Regional and Sanskrit sources - Rajatarangini, biographies, Vijayanagara and Qutb Shahi works

s: Tarikh-i-Firishta was dedicated to which ruler?
x: Muhammad Qasim Firishta dedicated Tarikh-i-Firishta, or Gulshan-i-Ibrahimi, to Ibrahim Adil Shah of Bijapur.
tq: Distinguish the dedicatee from the rulers whose dynasties are described in the work.
sec: Regional and Sanskrit sources - Rajatarangini, biographies, Vijayanagara and Qutb Shahi works

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with a Qutb Shahi source?
o: Tarikh Muhammad Qutb Shah — Mirza Ibrahim Zuberi
History of the Qutb Shahi Dynasty — Anonymous, 1617
x: Hadikat-us-Salatin was written by Ali bin Tahir Bustani and deals with the Qutb Shahis. Basatin-us-Salatin was by Mirza Ibrahim Zuberi, Tarikh Muhammad Qutb Shah is anonymous and dated 1617, while H.K. Sherwani wrote the modern history.
tq: Use the author–title pair as the anchor and eliminate shifted authorship and dates.
sec: Regional and Sanskrit sources - Rajatarangini, biographies, Vijayanagara and Qutb Shahi works

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Akbarnama was written by Abul Fazl. Tuzuk-i-Baburi was written by Babur, Humayun-nama by Gulbadan Begum and Padshahnama by Abdul Hamid Lahori.
tq: Use author–work matching and reject swapped authors.
sec: Royal memoirs and court histories → author

s: The Tuzuk-i-Baburi, also known as Baburnama, was written by Babur in which language?
x: Babur wrote the Tuzuk-i-Baburi in Turki. It is one of the important royal memoirs of the Mughal period.
tq: Test the exact language associated with a royal memoir.
sec: Royal memoirs and court histories → author

s: Who among the following authored the Humayun-nama?
x: Humayun-nama was authored by Gulbadan Begum, the daughter of Babur and sister of Humayun.
tq: Discriminate among closely associated Mughal court authors.
sec: Royal memoirs and court histories → author

s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri — Jahangir
2. Ain-i-Akbari — Abul Fazl
3. Padshahnama — Abdul Hamid Lahori
4. Humayun-nama — Gulbadan Begum
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri was written by Jahangir, Ain-i-Akbari by Abul Fazl, Padshahnama by Abdul Hamid Lahori and Humayun-nama by Gulbadan Begum.
tq: Verify each author–work pair before selecting the complete combination.
sec: Royal memoirs and court histories → author

s: Which of the following statements is correct regarding Mughal literary works and translations?
o: The Mahabharata was translated into Persian as Kalila wa Dimna.
The Panchatantra was translated into Persian as Ain-i-Akbari.
The Ramayana was translated into Persian as Padshahnama.
The Mahabharata was translated into Persian as Razmnama.
x: The Persian translation of the Mahabharata was known as Razmnama. Kalila wa Dimna was the Persian rendering of the Panchatantra.
tq: Separate translated works from the titles of their Persian versions.
sec: Royal memoirs and court histories → author

s: The Ain-i-Akbari, dated to 1590, contains an early reference to which festival?
x: The Ain-i-Akbari, dated to 1590, mentions Diwali. This makes it an important early textual reference to the festival.
tq: Link the precise date with the cultural fact rather than a nearby festival.
sec: Royal memoirs and court histories → author

s: The Ghazinagar Persian inscription is located in which present-day district, and is associated with which Qutb Shahi ruler?
o: Medak district — Jamsheed Quli Qutb Shah
Warangal district — Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah
x: The Ghazinagar inscription is in Nalgonda and is associated with Ibrahim Quli. It dates to 1576–77.
tq: Combine location, ruler and date in an inscription-based identification.
sec: Inscriptions and coins as medieval sources

s: Which of the following correctly lists the Qutb Shahi inscriptions and their dates?
x: The Daru-Shifa inscription dates to 1595, while the Badshahi Ashurkhana inscription dates to 1592–96. The other dates belong to different records.
tq: Match inscriptions with their exact dates and avoid date swapping.
sec: Inscriptions and coins as medieval sources

s: The Nizami Mosque inscription at Golconda is significant because it dates Quli Qutb-ul-Mulk's independence to:
x: The Nizami Mosque inscription at Golconda dates the independence of Quli Qutb-ul-Mulk to 1518.
tq: Test the precise date attached to a political event in an inscription.
sec: Inscriptions and coins as medieval sources

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Vilasa copper plate — Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka
Palam Baoli inscription — Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka
x: The Palam Baoli inscription is a Sanskrit record praising Balban and dates to 1276. The Vilasa copper plate is associated with Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka.
tq: Find the wrongly assigned person by checking the inscription–issuer relationship.
sec: Inscriptions and coins as medieval sources

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Vilasa copper plate is associated with Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka.
2. The Kaluvacheru inscription is associated with Anitalli.
3. The Warangal inscription of Shitab Khan dates to 1504–06.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. The Vilasa copper plate dates approximately to 1330, the Kaluvacheru record is associated with Anitalli, and Shitab Khan's Warangal inscription dates to 1504–06.
tq: Check names, record types and dates independently before choosing the combination.
sec: Inscriptions and coins as medieval sources

s: Mahmud of Ghazni's Lahore dirhams are especially significant as medieval sources because they contain:
o: An Arabic legend and its Sanskrit translation in Sharada script
A Telugu inscription and an Arabic translation
A Sanskrit legend and its Persian translation in Devanagari script
Only a Persian inscription in Nastaliq script
x: The Lahore dirhams of Mahmud of Ghazni carry an Arabic legend along with a Sanskrit translation written in Sharada script.
tq: Use the script–language combination to distinguish bilingual numismatic evidence.
sec: Inscriptions and coins as medieval sources

s: The Palam Baoli inscription of 1276 praises which ruler in Sanskrit?
x: The Palam Baoli inscription, dated 1276, praises Balban in Sanskrit.
tq: Link the inscription's date with the ruler praised in it.
sec: Inscriptions and coins as medieval sources

s: Which of the following correctly describes the coinage of Iltutmish?
o: He replaced the silver tanka with a copper jital as the sole coin.
He issued purely Arabic coinage consisting of silver tankas and copper jitals.
He issued only gold coins with Sanskrit legends.
He introduced bilingual dirhams with Telugu and Arabic legends.
x: Iltutmish issued purely Arabic coinage, including the silver tanka and the copper jital.
tq: Distinguish the coin issuer, metal and script from nearby numismatic facts.
sec: Inscriptions and coins as medieval sources

s: The transition from trabeate to arcuate construction in Sultanate architecture is marked by the increasing use of:
o: Wooden pillars and flat roofs only
Timber frames and corbelled balconies only
True arches, domes and lime mortar
x: Sultanate buildings demonstrate the shift from trabeate construction to arcuate construction through the use of true arches, domes and lime mortar.
tq: Identify the architectural system from its characteristic structural elements.
sec: Architecture and paintings as sources

s: Which monument is regarded as the first true application of Islamic architectural principles in the Delhi Sultanate?
x: The Alai Darwaza is regarded as the first true application of Islamic architectural principles in the Sultanate period.
tq: Distinguish a specific architectural landmark from other Sultanate monuments.
sec: Architecture and paintings as sources

s:
With reference to Qutb Shahi calligraphy, consider the following statements:
1. Naskh was used for Quranic verses, including those in the Jami Masjid mihrab.
2. Nastaliq was used for Persian texts.
3. Naskh and Nastaliq were forms of architectural construction.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Naskh was used for Quranic verses, while Nastaliq was used for Persian texts. They are calligraphic scripts, not forms of architectural construction.
tq: Separate the two related scripts from the unrelated architectural term.
sec: Architecture and paintings as sources

s: Who founded the Golconda school of painting?
x: The Golconda school of painting was founded by Mir Hashimi.
tq: Test the founder of an artistic tradition against prominent literary figures.
sec: Architecture and paintings as sources

s: The manuscript titled “Quliyat Quli” is noted for containing how many miniatures?
x: The Quliyat Quli manuscript contains 14 miniatures.
tq: Recall the exact numerical detail associated with an art source.
sec: Architecture and paintings as sources

s: Which of the following statements correctly reflects the nature of court histories in medieval India?
o: They avoided all religious and political viewpoints.
They were entirely independent of royal patronage.
They were written exclusively by foreign travellers.
They generally glorified the ruler who patronised the writer.
x: Court histories were influenced by royal patronage and generally glorified the patron ruler. Their authors could also reflect particular religious or political viewpoints.
tq: Apply the source-criticism principle of patronage bias.
sec: Chronicle writers' biases - court patronage, religious viewpoint

s: Who wrote the official history of Akbar and was one of Akbar's Navaratnas?
x: Abul Fazl wrote the official history of Akbar and was one of Akbar's Navaratnas.
tq: Identify the court historian through both office and patronage association.
sec: Chronicle writers' biases - court patronage, religious viewpoint

s: Which one of the following correctly describes Ziauddin Barani?
o: He wrote from an orthodox Sunni viewpoint and theorised kingship.
He was a Persian ambassador to Vijayanagara and described its markets.
He founded the Golconda school of painting.
He composed the royal memoirs of Jahangir.
x: Ziauddin Barani wrote from an orthodox Sunni viewpoint and also theorised about kingship. The other descriptions belong to different figures or traditions.
tq: Use the writer's viewpoint and intellectual contribution to identify him.
sec: Chronicle writers' biases - court patronage, religious viewpoint

s: Amir Khusrau's position in the Sultanate literary tradition is best described as that of a:
x: Amir Khusrau was a court poet. His accounts, along with those of Wassaf, recorded five invasions of Warangal.
tq: Match a famous medieval personality with his primary court role.
sec: Chronicle writers' biases - court patronage, religious viewpoint

s: Telugu sources and Muslim sources differ in their accounts of the number of invasions of Warangal. Which statement is correct?
o: Telugu sources record 5 invasions, while Muslim sources record 8.
Telugu sources record 8 invasions, while Muslim sources record 5.
Both groups of sources record 8 invasions.
Both groups of sources record 5 invasions.
x: The Telugu sources Pratapa Charitra, Vilasa and Kaluvacheru record eight invasions of Warangal, whereas Muslim sources associated with Amir Khusrau and Wassaf record five.
tq: Compare conflicting numerical claims by source tradition.
sec: Chronicle writers' biases - court patronage, religious viewpoint

s: Which of the following statements regarding Firishta's account of Deva Raya is correct?
o: His story that Deva Raya kidnapped Nehal has been rejected by modern historians.
Modern historians regard Firishta as the author of the Ain-i-Akbari.
His story that Deva Raya kidnapped Nehal is accepted without reservation by modern historians.
Firishta did not write about Deva Raya.
x: Firishta's story that Deva Raya kidnapped Nehal is rejected by modern historians. This illustrates the need to critically evaluate chronicle narratives.
tq: Identify the historically qualified statement rather than accepting a dramatic anecdote.
sec: Chronicle writers' biases - court patronage, religious viewpoint

s: Foreign travellers' accounts of medieval India should generally be used by historians in which manner?
o: They should replace inscriptions and archaeological evidence.
They should be ignored because they were written outside India.
They should be accepted as accurate in every detail.
They should supplement Indian texts and be cross-verified with inscriptions and archaeology.
x: Foreign accounts supplement Indian textual evidence, but their statements must be cross-verified with inscriptions and archaeological evidence.
tq: Apply the principle of corroboration across different source types.
sec: Chronicle writers' biases - court patronage, religious viewpoint

s: Which of the following combinations correctly associates an AP-linked source with the place or polity described?
o: Marco Polo — Motupalli; Abdur Razzaq — Vijayanagara; Tavernier — Golconda
Marco Polo — Golconda; Abdur Razzaq — Warangal; Tavernier — Motupalli
Barbosa — Motupalli; Isami — Vijayanagara; Firishta — Golconda
Tavernier — Vijayanagara; Marco Polo — Warangal; Barbosa — Golconda
x: Marco Polo is associated with Motupalli, Abdur Razzaq and Barbosa with Vijayanagara, and Tavernier with Golconda. Isami and Firishta are associated with Warangal.
tq: Start with the sure place–traveller pair and complete the matching set.
sec: Universal angles

s: Which of the following set of sources is cited as early evidence of Diwali in the context of its UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage discussion?
x: Al-Biruni, Nicolo Conti and the Ain-i-Akbari are cited as early evidence of Diwali in the referenced UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage discussion.
tq: Distinguish the exact evidence set from other medieval source combinations.
sec: Universal angles

s: In the suit claiming that the Taj Mahal was a temple, the Allahabad High Court sought responses from which authorities?
o: The UNESCO and the World Bank
The Centre and the Archaeological Survey of India
The Centre and the Reserve Bank of India
The Election Commission and the Archaeological Survey of India
x: The Allahabad High Court sought responses from the Centre and the Archaeological Survey of India. The evidence that Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal rests on chronicles, records and European travellers' accounts.
tq: Identify the institutions involved by separating them from unrelated constitutional and international bodies.
sec: Universal angles
